title: Integration mix
unit: IAL Pure Mathematics (P4); mark the unit as inferred

questions.question: Using the substitution u = sqrt(2x + 1), show that the integral from 4 to 12 of sqrt(8x + 4) e^(sqrt(2x + 1)) dx may be expressed in the form the integral from a to b of k u^2 e^u du, where a, b and k are constants to be found.
steps: From u^2 = 2x + 1: x = (u^2 - 1)/2 and dx = u du.
The integrand becomes 2u e^u x u du = 2u^2 e^u du.
Limits: x = 4 gives u = 3; x = 12 gives u = 5. So a = 3, b = 5, k = 2.

questions.question: Hence find, by algebraic integration, the exact value of the integral from 4 to 12 of sqrt(8x + 4) e^(sqrt(2x + 1)) dx, giving your answer in simplest form.
steps: By parts twice, the integral of u^2 e^u du is e^u (u^2 - 2u + 2) + c.
Check by differentiating: e^u(u^2 - 2u + 2) + e^u(2u - 2) = u^2 e^u.
Evaluate the integral of 2u^2 e^u from 3 to 5 as 2[e^u(u^2 - 2u + 2)].

questions.question: Find the integral of e^(2x) sin x dx.
questions.answer: e^(2x)(2 sin x - cos x)/5 + c
steps: Let I = integral of e^(2x) sin x dx. Parts with u = e^(2x), dv = sin x dx: I = -e^(2x) cos x + 2 integral of e^(2x) cos x dx.
Parts again on the new integral: integral of e^(2x) cos x dx = e^(2x) sin x - 2I.
So I = -e^(2x) cos x + 2e^(2x) sin x - 4I, giving 5I = e^(2x)(2 sin x - cos x).
Therefore I = e^(2x)(2 sin x - cos x)/5 + c.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows part of the curve y = e^(2x) sin x, x >= 0. The finite region R is bounded by the curve and the x-axis. Show that the exact area of R is (e^(2pi) + 1)/5.
steps: The curve next meets the x-axis at x = pi, and sin x >= 0 on [0, pi].
Area = integral from 0 to pi of e^(2x) sin x dx.
Using part (a): [e^(2x)(2 sin x - cos x)/5] from 0 to pi.

questions.question: Use integration by parts to find the exact value of the integral from 0 to 4 of x^2 e^(2x) dx, giving your answer in simplest form.
steps: Parts with u = x^2, dv = e^(2x) dx: integral = x^2 e^(2x)/2 - integral of x e^(2x) dx.
Parts again on x e^(2x): integral = x e^(2x)/2 - e^(2x)/4.
So the antiderivative is e^(2x)(x^2/2 - x/2 + 1/4). Check: differentiating gives x^2 e^(2x).

questions.question: Use integration by substitution to show that the integral from 3 to 21/2 of 4x/(2x - 1)^2 dx = a + ln b, where a and b are constants to be found.
steps: Let u = 2x - 1, so x = (u + 1)/2 and dx = du/2.
4x = 2(u + 1), so the integrand becomes 2(u + 1)/u^2 x du/2 = (u + 1)/u^2 du = (1/u + 1/u^2) du.
Limits: x = 3 gives u = 5; x = 21/2 gives u = 20.
Integrate: [ln u - 1/u] from 5 to 20.

questions.question: Find the integral of x^2 e^x dx.
steps: Parts with u = x^2, dv = e^x dx: integral = x^2 e^x - 2 integral of x e^x dx.
Parts on x e^x: integral = x e^x - e^x.
So integral = x^2 e^x - 2x e^x + 2e^x + c.
Factorise: e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2) + c.

questions.question: Use the substitution u = sqrt(1 - 3x) to show that the integral of 27x/sqrt(1 - 3x) dx = -2(1 - 3x)^(1/2)(Ax + B) + k, where A and B are integers to be found and k is an arbitrary constant.
steps: From u^2 = 1 - 3x: x = (1 - u^2)/3 and dx = -(2u/3) du.
The integrand becomes 9(1 - u^2)/u x (-(2u/3)) du = -6(1 - u^2) du.
Integrate: -6u + 2u^3 + k.
Write -2u(Ax + B) = -2u(A(1 - u^2)/3 + B). With A = 3, B = 2 this is -2u(3 - u^2) = -6u + 2u^3, which matches.

questions.question: Using the substitution u = 3 + sqrt(2x - 1), find the exact value of the integral from 1 to 13 of 4/(3 + sqrt(2x - 1)) dx, giving your answer in the form p + q ln 2, where p and q are integers.
steps: Let s = sqrt(2x - 1), so x = (s^2 + 1)/2 and dx = s ds.
With u = 3 + s: s = u - 3 and dx = (u - 3) du.
Limits: x = 1 gives u = 4; x = 13 gives s = 5 and u = 8.
Integral = integral from 4 to 8 of 4(u - 3)/u du = 4 integral of (1 - 3/u) du.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows the curve y = 16 sin 2x/(3 + 4 sin x)^2, 0 <= x <= pi/2. The region R is bounded by the curve, the x-axis and the line x = pi/6. Using the substitution u = 3 + 4 sin x, show that the area of R can be written as a + ln b, where a and b are rational constants to be found.
steps: Use sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x, and du = 4 cos x dx, so 16 sin 2x dx = 32 sin x cos x dx = 8 sin x du.
Since sin x = (u - 3)/4, this is 2(u - 3) du, and (3 + 4 sin x)^2 = u^2.
The integrand becomes 2(u - 3)/u^2 = 2/u - 6/u^2.
Limits: x = pi/6 gives u = 5; x = pi/2 gives u = 7.

questions.question: Use the substitution x = 2 sin u to show that the integral from 0 to 1 of (3x + 2)/(4 - x^2)^(3/2) dx = integral from 0 to p of ((3/2) sec u tan u + (1/2) sec^2 u) du, where p is a constant to be found. (The scan shows no mark for this part; the question total of 4 is all taken by part (b). Marks here are set to 0.)
steps: x = 2 sin u gives dx = 2 cos u du and 4 - x^2 = 4 cos^2 u, so (4 - x^2)^(3/2) = 8 cos^3 u.
Integrand: (6 sin u + 2)(2 cos u)/(8 cos^3 u) = (3/2) sin u/cos^2 u + (1/2)/cos^2 u.
This equals (3/2) sec u tan u + (1/2) sec^2 u.
Limits: x = 0 gives u = 0; x = 1 gives sin u = 1/2, so u = pi/6. Hence p = pi/6.

questions.question: Hence find the exact value of the integral from 0 to 1 of (3x + 2)/(4 - x^2)^(3/2) dx.
steps: Antiderivative: (3/2) sec u + (1/2) tan u, since d/du sec u = sec u tan u and d/du tan u = sec^2 u.
At u = pi/6: sec = 2/sqrt(3), tan = 1/sqrt(3), giving sqrt(3) + sqrt(3)/6 = 7 sqrt(3)/6.

questions.question: Find the integral of ln x / x^2 dx.
steps: Parts with u = ln x and dv = x^(-2) dx, so v = -1/x.
Integral = -ln x/x + integral of (1/x)(1/x) dx = -ln x/x + integral of x^(-2) dx.
= -ln x/x - 1/x + c = -(ln x + 1)/x + c.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows part of the curve y = (3 + 2x + ln x)/x^2, x > 0.5. The region R is bounded by the curve, the line x = 2, the x-axis and the line x = 4. Use the answer to part (a) to find the exact area of R, in simplest form.
steps: Split the integrand: y = 3/x^2 + 2/x + ln x/x^2.
Integral from 2 to 4 of 3/x^2 dx = [-3/x] = -3/4 + 3/2 = 3/4.
Integral from 2 to 4 of 2/x dx = 2 ln 2.
Using part (a): integral of ln x/x^2 from 2 to 4 = [-(ln x + 1)/x] = (ln 2 + 1)/2 - (2 ln 2 + 1)/4 = 1/4.
Total area = 3/4 + 2 ln 2 + 1/4 = 1 + 2 ln 2.

questions.question: Using a suitable substitution, find, using calculus, the value of the integral from 1 to 5 of 3x/sqrt(2x - 1) dx.
steps: Let s = sqrt(2x - 1), so x = (s^2 + 1)/2 and dx = s ds.
The integrand becomes 3x/s x s ds = (3/2)(s^2 + 1) ds.
Limits: x = 1 gives s = 1; x = 5 gives s = 3.
Value = 16.

questions.question: Find the integral of (6x^2 - 16)/((x + 1)(2x - 3)) dx.
steps: Numerator and denominator have the same degree, so divide: 6x^2 - 16 = 3(2x^2 - x - 3) + (3x - 7).
The integrand is 3 + (3x - 7)/((x + 1)(2x - 3)).
Integrate: 3x + 2 ln|x + 1| - (1/2) ln|2x - 3| + c.

questions.question: Use algebraic integration and the substitution u = sqrt(x) to find the exact value of the integral from 1 to 4 of 10/(5x + 2x sqrt(x)) dx. Write your answer in the form 4 ln(a/b), where a and b are integers.
steps: Let u = sqrt(x), so x = u^2 and dx = 2u du.
Denominator: 5u^2 + 2u^3 = u^2(5 + 2u), so the integrand becomes 20u/(u^2(5 + 2u)) du = 20/(u(5 + 2u)) du.
Partial fractions: 1/(u(5 + 2u)) = (1/5)(1/u - 2/(5 + 2u)), so the integrand is 4/u - 8/(5 + 2u).
Integrate: 4 ln u - 4 ln(5 + 2u) = 4 ln(u/(5 + 2u)).
Limits: x = 1 gives u = 1; x = 4 gives u = 2. Value = 4[ln(2/9) - ln(1/7)] = 4 ln(14/9).

questions.question: Figure 2 shows part of the curve y = 4x - x e^(x/2), x >= 0. The curve meets the x-axis at the origin O and cuts it at the point A. Find, in terms of ln 2, the x coordinate of A.
steps: On the x-axis y = 0: x(4 - e^(x/2)) = 0.
x > 0 (A is not O), so e^(x/2) = 4.
x/2 = ln 4, so x = 2 ln 4 = 4 ln 2.

questions.question: Find the integral of x e^(x/2) dx.
steps: Parts with u = x and dv = e^(x/2) dx, so v = 2e^(x/2).
Integral = 2x e^(x/2) - integral of 2e^(x/2) dx = 2x e^(x/2) - 4e^(x/2) + c.
Factorise: 2e^(x/2)(x - 2) + c.

questions.question: The finite region R, shown shaded in Figure 2, is bounded by the x-axis and the curve y = 4x - x e^(x/2), x >= 0. Find, by integration, the exact area of R, giving your answer in terms of ln 2.
steps: Area = integral from 0 to A of (4x - x e^(x/2)) dx, where A = 4 ln 2.
Integral of 4x is 2x^2; at A this gives 2(4 ln 2)^2 = 32(ln 2)^2.
Using part (b): integral of x e^(x/2) from 0 to A = [2e^(x/2)(x - 2)] = 2(4)(A - 2) - 2(1)(-2) = 8A - 12 = 32 ln 2 - 12.
So the area is 32(ln 2)^2 - 32 ln 2 + 12.

questions.question: Find the derivative with respect to y of 1/(1 + 2 ln y)^2.
steps: Write the function as (1 + 2 ln y)^(-2).
Simplify: -4/(y(1 + 2 ln y)^3).

questions.question: Hence find a general solution to the differential equation 3 cosec(2x) dy/dx = y(1 + 2 ln y)^3, where y > 0 and -pi/2 < x < pi/2.
steps: Rearrange: dy/dx = (1/3) sin 2x x y(1 + 2 ln y)^3, so dy/(y(1 + 2 ln y)^3) = (1/3) sin 2x dx.
By part (a), the left side integrates to -1/(4(1 + 2 ln y)^2).
The right side integrates to -(1/6) cos 2x.
So 1/(1 + 2 ln y)^2 = (2/3) cos 2x + C, where C is an arbitrary constant.

questions.question: Show that the particular solution of the differential equation in part (b) for which y = 1 at x = pi/6 is given by y = e^(A sec x - 1/2), where A is an irrational number to be found.
questions.answer: A = sqrt(3)/4, so y = e^((sqrt(3)/4) sec x - 1/2)
steps: Use the general solution from (b): 1/(1 + 2 ln y)^2 = (2/3) cos 2x + C.
(1 + 2 ln y)^2 = (3/4) sec^2 x; take the positive root (it gives 1 at x = pi/6, where sec x = 2/sqrt(3)): 1 + 2 ln y = (sqrt(3)/2) sec x.
ln y = (sqrt(3)/4) sec x - 1/2, so y = e^(A sec x - 1/2) with A = sqrt(3)/4 (irrational).

questions.question: f(x) = (8x - 5)/((2x - 1)(4x - 3)), x > 1. Express f(x) in partial fractions.
Hence find the integral of f(x) dx, where f(x) = (8x - 5)/((2x - 1)(4x - 3)) and x > 1.
steps: Integral of 1/(2x - 1) is (1/2) ln(2x - 1).
Both factors are positive for x > 1, so the sum is (1/2) ln((2x - 1)(4x - 3)) + c.

questions.question: Use the answer to part (b) to find the value of k for which the integral from k to 3k of f(x) dx = (1/2) ln 20.
steps: Set the ratio equal to 20: (6k - 1)(12k - 3) = 20(2k - 1)(4k - 3).
f is defined for x > 1, so k > 1 and k = 3/2.

questions.question: Use the substitution u = e^x - 3 to show that the integral from ln 5 to ln 7 of 4e^(3x)/(e^x - 3) dx = a + b ln 2, where a and b are constants to be found.
steps: du = e^x dx, and e^(3x) = e^(2x) e^x with e^(2x) = (u + 3)^2.
So the integrand becomes 4(u + 3)^2/u du.
Expand: 4(u + 6 + 9/u) du.
Limits: x = ln 5 gives u = 2; x = ln 7 gives u = 4.
Integral = 4[u^2/2 + 6u + 9 ln u] from 2 to 4 = 4(18 + 9 ln 2) = 72 + 36 ln 2.

questions.question: Show, by integration, that the integral of 3e^x cos 2x dx = p e^x sin 2x + q e^x cos 2x + c, where p and q are constants to be found and c is an arbitrary constant.
steps: Differentiate the right side: p(e^x sin 2x + 2 e^x cos 2x) + q(e^x cos 2x - 2 e^x sin 2x).
Collect: e^x[(p - 2q) sin 2x + (2p + q) cos 2x].
Match with 3e^x cos 2x: p - 2q = 0 and 2p + q = 3.
Solve: p = 2q, so 5q = 3, giving q = 3/5 and p = 6/5.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows the curve with parametric equations x = sqrt(9 - 4t), y = t^3/sqrt(9 + 4t), 0 <= t <= 9/4. The region R is bounded by the curve, the x-axis and the y-axis. Show that the area of R is given by K integral from 0 to 9/4 of t^3/sqrt(81 - 16t^2) dt, where K is a constant to be found.
steps: Area = integral of y dx over x from 0 to 3 = integral of y (-dx/dt) dt over t from 0 to 9/4.
dx/dt = -2/sqrt(9 - 4t), so -dx/dt = 2/sqrt(9 - 4t).
Area = integral of 2t^3/(sqrt(9 + 4t) sqrt(9 - 4t)) dt.
Since (9 + 4t)(9 - 4t) = 81 - 16t^2, area = 2 integral of t^3/sqrt(81 - 16t^2) dt, so K = 2.

questions.question: Using the substitution u = 81 - 16t^2, or otherwise, find the exact area of R. (Calculator solutions are not acceptable.)
steps: Limits: t = 0 gives u = 81; t = 9/4 gives u = 0.
Area = 2 integral of t^3/sqrt(u) dt = -(1/256) integral from 81 to 0 of (81 - u)u^(-1/2) du = (1/256) integral from 0 to 81 of (81u^(-1/2) - u^(1/2)) du.

questions.question: Express 1/((1 + 3x)(1 - x)) in partial fractions.
steps: Put x = 1: 1 = 4B, so B = 1/4.

questions.question: Hence find the solution of the differential equation (1 + 3x)(1 - x) dy/dx = tan y, -1/3 < x <= 1/2, for which x = 1/2 when y = pi/2. Give your answer in the form sin^n y = f(x), where n is an integer to be found.
steps: Integrate: ln(sin y) = (1/4) ln(1 + 3x) - (1/4) ln(1 - x) + C.
Multiply by 4: sin^4 y = K(1 + 3x)/(1 - x).
Substitute x = 1/2, y = pi/2 (sin y = 1): 1 = K(5/2)/(1/2) = 5K, so K = 1/5.
Hence sin^4 y = (1 + 3x)/(5(1 - x)), so n = 4.

questions.question: f(x) = 1/(x(3x - 1)^2) = A/x + B/(3x - 1) + C/(3x - 1)^2. Find the values of the constants A, B and C.
steps: Multiply out: 1 = A(3x - 1)^2 + Bx(3x - 1) + Cx.
Put x = 0: A = 1. Put x = 1/3: 1 = C/3, so C = 3.
Compare x^2 coefficients: 9A + 3B = 0, so B = -3.
Check the x coefficient: -6A - B + C = -6 + 3 + 3 = 0.

questions.question: Hence find the integral of f(x) dx, where f(x) = 1/(x(3x - 1)^2). (The scan shows no mark for part (i); the question total of 10 is taken by parts (a) and (b)(ii). Marks here are set to 0.)
steps: Integrate A/x: ln|x|.
Integrate -3/(3x - 1): -ln|3x - 1|.

questions.topic: Definite Integral Form a Plus ln b
questions.question: Find the integral from 1 to 2 of f(x) dx, where f(x) = 1/(x(3x - 1)^2), giving your answer in the form a + ln b, where a and b are constants.
steps: Antiderivative F(x) = ln(x/(3x - 1)) - 1/(3x - 1).

questions.question: Figures 3 and 4 show a doorknob formed by rotating the curve f(x) = (1/4)(4 - x)e^x, 0 <= x <= 4, through 360 degrees about the x-axis (units in cm). Show that the volume V cm^3 is given by V = K integral from 0 to 4 of (x^2 - 8x + 16)e^(2x) dx, where K is a constant to be found.
steps: Volume = pi integral from 0 to 4 of y^2 dx, with y^2 = (1/16)(4 - x)^2 e^(2x).
So V = (pi/16) integral of (x^2 - 8x + 16) e^(2x) dx, giving K = pi/16.

questions.question: Hence, find the exact value of the volume of the doorknob. Give your answer in the form p pi (e^q + r) cm^3, where p, q and r are simplified rational numbers.
steps: Antiderivative of g(x) e^(2x), where g = x^2 - 8x + 16: e^(2x)[(x^2 - 9x + 20)/2 + 1/4].
Check by differentiating: e^(2x)[x^2 - 8x + 16].
At x = 4 the bracket is 0 + 1/4 = 1/4; at x = 0 it is 10 + 1/4 = 41/4.
